question: Can the finite-helix correction alone account for all four resolved disagreements?
other_parameters: Fixed published stationary parameters from current benchmark; no tuning to labels
discriminating_rule: If any of the four baseline disagreements remains under both variants at320steps, helix omission alone cannot explain all four. Report every resolved row, not only improved cases.
scope: Single assistant reviewed25-row subset; source coordinates inherited; no population accuracy, no independent physical validation

base_config.parameter_location: Published Table 1 (p774); Sec3 (p773); force convention Eqs2-7; Fig7 p776 up-milling labels digitized in existing repository CSV
base_config.evaluation: Only25 visually resolved rows from fixed-seed32-row stratified audit, after correcting the assistants own three premature cross identifications. All resolved rows retained regardless of model agreement. No fitting, no full516 accuracy claim.
base_config.uncertainty: Same-assistant review, some prior exposure, revision2 corrected annotation mistakes. Not independent blinded annotation. Coordinates inherited. Old516 CSV contains at least one clear wrong label and boundary markers;68.41% is old-label agreement only. Current25-row subset is provisional.
base_config.limits: Stationary diagonal modal parameters; paper reports speed-dependent frequency and likely cutting-coefficient variation. No process damping, tool runout, mode coupling in measured FRF, or nonlinear contact. Constant coefficients not fitted to improve accuracy.
